subsections: Plan vs non-plan expenditure - items and end of the classification

accepted.s:
Under the erstwhile Plan and non-Plan classification of government expenditure, Plan expenditure comprised:
1. Expenditure on Central Plans
2. Central assistance for State and Union Territory Plans
3. Interest payments on public debt
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Plan expenditure covered Central Plans and central assistance for State and Union Territory Plans. Interest payments were classified as non-Plan expenditure.
accepted.tq: Separate the two components of the former Plan category from a familiar non-Plan item.
accepted.sec: Plan vs non-plan expenditure - items and end of the classification  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following was a non-Plan expenditure item under the former classification?
o: Expenditure on a new Central Plan
Central assistance for Union Territory Plans
accepted.x: Interest payments formed part of the larger non-Plan expenditure category. Central Plans and central assistance for State and Union Territory Plans were Plan expenditure.
accepted.tq: Use the direct association between interest payments and the former non-Plan category.
accepted.sec: Plan vs non-plan expenditure - items and end of the classification  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following sets contains only items classified as non-Plan expenditure under the former system?
o: Interest payments, defence, subsidies, salaries and pensions
Central Plans, defence, subsidies, salaries and pensions
Central assistance for State Plans, pensions, salaries and interest payments
Central Plans, Central assistance for Union Territory Plans and defence
accepted.x: Interest payments, defence, subsidies, salaries, pensions and maintenance of assets created in earlier Plans were non-Plan items. Central Plans and central assistance for State or Union Territory Plans were Plan items.
accepted.tq: Check every item in a set against the former classification rather than identifying only one familiar item.
accepted.sec: Plan vs non-plan expenditure - items and end of the classification  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The classification of expenditure into Plan and non-Plan was discontinued from which Budget year?
accepted.x: The Plan and non-Plan classification ended from Budget 2017-18 on the recommendation of the Expenditure Management Commission.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the discontinuation year from adjacent Budget years.
accepted.sec: Plan vs non-plan expenditure - items and end of the classification  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Plan and non-Plan classification was replaced primarily by which classification?
accepted.x: After the discontinuation of Plan and non-Plan expenditure, the revenue-capital classification became the principal framework.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between two different expenditure classifications that are commonly interchanged.
accepted.sec: Plan vs non-plan expenditure - items and end of the classification  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about the Union Budget changes associated with the end of Plan and non-Plan classification is correct?
o: The Railway Budget was abolished and the Budget was presented on 15 August.
The Railway Budget was merged with the Union Budget and the Budget was presented on 31 March.
The Railway Budget was separated and the Budget was presented on 1 April.
The Railway Budget was merged with the Union Budget and the Budget was presented on 1 February.
accepted.x: The relevant Budget changes included the merger of the Railway Budget with the Union Budget and presentation of the Union Budget on 1 February.
accepted.tq: Pair the two associated procedural changes instead of selecting only one of them.
accepted.sec: Plan vs non-plan expenditure - items and end of the classification  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding developmental and non-developmental expenditure:
List-I (Category)
 a. Developmental expenditure
 b. Non-developmental expenditure
 c. Economic and social services
 d. Routine operational spending
List-II (Description)
 i. Defence, interest payments and pensions
 ii. Education, health, irrigation and agriculture
 iii. A component of developmental expenditure
 iv. Consumptive expenditure required for routine operations
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Developmental expenditure includes education, health, irrigation and agriculture; non-developmental expenditure includes defence, interest payments and pensions. Economic and social services are developmental, while routine operational spending is consumptive.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure pair linking education and health to developmental expenditure.
accepted.sec: Developmental vs non-developmental expenditure - classifying items  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT generally classified as developmental expenditure?
accepted.x: Defence is classified as non-developmental expenditure. Rural development, social welfare and public health are developmental activities.
accepted.tq: Find the item outside the growth and quality-of-life group.
accepted.sec: Developmental vs non-developmental expenditure - classifying items  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding developmental expenditure:
1. It includes expenditure on education and health.
2. It includes expenditure on employment and rural development.
3. It is intended to stimulate growth, employment and quality of life.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements correctly describe developmental expenditure and its principal objectives.
accepted.tq: Recognise that the functional list and the stated economic purpose belong to the same category.
accepted.sec: Developmental vs non-developmental expenditure - classifying items  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following combinations consists entirely of non-developmental expenditure items?
o: Interest payments, police and law and order, tax-collection charges
Employment, rural development and public health
accepted.x: Interest payments, police and law and order, tax-collection charges and administrative expenditure are non-developmental items.
accepted.tq: Classify the entire combination, not merely the first item.
accepted.sec: Developmental vs non-developmental expenditure - classifying items  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Assertion (A): Developmental expenditure is associated with improvement in employment and quality of life.
Reason (R): It includes economic and social services such as education, health, irrigation and rural development.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
accepted.x: Both statements are true, and the inclusion of economic and social services explains why developmental expenditure improves employment and quality of life.
accepted.tq: Test whether the functional examples in the Reason explain the stated outcome in the Assertion.
accepted.sec: Developmental vs non-developmental expenditure - classifying items  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with the revenue-capital classification?
o: Maintenance of existing assets — Capital expenditure
Loans and advances to States — Capital expenditure
accepted.x: Loans and advances to States are capital expenditure because they affect the Government's financial assets. Maintenance of existing assets and interest payments are revenue expenditure, while repayment of loans reduces liabilities and is capital expenditure.
accepted.tq: Use the effect on assets or liabilities to identify the correct classification.
accepted.sec: Revenue vs capital expenditure - classifying items  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A government expenditure creates a new asset or reduces an existing liability. Under the revenue-capital distinction, it is ordinarily treated as:
accepted.x: Capital expenditure either creates assets or reduces liabilities. Revenue expenditure generally neither creates an asset nor reduces a liability.
accepted.tq: Apply the asset-liability test instead of relying on the department incurring the expenditure.
accepted.sec: Revenue vs capital expenditure - classifying items  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Grants to State governments remain revenue expenditure even if the States use them to create assets.
2. Purchase of defence equipment can be capital outlay.
3. Subsidies are ordinarily classified as capital expenditure because they support production.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Grants to State governments are revenue expenditure even when they create assets for the States, and defence equipment can be capital outlay. Subsidies are revenue expenditure, not capital expenditure.
accepted.tq: Identify the exception concerning grants and reject the reversed treatment of subsidies.
accepted.sec: Revenue vs capital expenditure - classifying items  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is correctly classified as revenue expenditure?
o: Loan advanced to a public sector undertaking
accepted.x: Maintenance of existing assets is revenue expenditure. Construction of an airport, repayment of loans and loans to public sector undertakings are capital expenditure.
accepted.tq: Distinguish ordinary maintenance from expenditure that creates assets or reduces liabilities.
accepted.sec: Revenue vs capital expenditure - classifying items  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is an example of an implicit or hidden subsidy?
o: A fertiliser subsidy shown in the Budget
An export incentive shown as a Budget provision
A food subsidy shown as a separate Budget line item
Under-pricing of higher education in a public university
accepted.x: Under-pricing of publicly provided services, such as higher education in public universities, is an implicit or hidden subsidy. Food, fertiliser and export incentives shown in the Budget are explicit subsidies.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a visible Budget line item from under-pricing of a publicly provided service.
accepted.sec: Subsidies - major heads, explicit vs hidden, NBS, Oil Pool Account  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following sets contains only explicit subsidies?
o: Food, fertiliser, LPG and interest subvention
Public university education, irrigation water and public health
Irrigation water, LPG and higher education
accepted.x: Food, fertiliser, LPG, export incentives and interest subvention are explicit subsidies because they are shown as Budget line items. The other listed services are examples of hidden subsidies when under-priced.
accepted.tq: Use the visibility-in-the-Budget test to separate explicit from hidden subsidies.
accepted.sec: Subsidies - major heads, explicit vs hidden, NBS, Oil Pool Account  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the Nutrient Based Subsidy scheme, subsidy is fixed with reference to:
o: The quantity of food grains procured by the Government
The quantity of specified nutrients in decontrolled P&K fertilisers
The retail price of urea alone
The international price of crude oil
accepted.x: NBS fixes subsidy per kilogram of nutrient in decontrolled phosphorus- and potassium-based fertilisers. Urea is outside the NBS framework.
accepted.tq: Link the scheme name to its nutrient-based calculation rather than to the price of a single fertiliser.
accepted.sec: Subsidies - major heads, explicit vs hidden, NBS, Oil Pool Account  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Nutrient Based Subsidy scheme was introduced from:
accepted.x: The Nutrient Based Subsidy scheme commenced on 1 April 2010.
accepted.tq: Discriminate the notified commencement date from adjacent years.
accepted.sec: Subsidies - major heads, explicit vs hidden, NBS, Oil Pool Account  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Nutrient Based Subsidy scheme is correct?
o: It covers only urea and excludes all P&K fertilisers.
It covers 22 grades, including DAP, MOP and SSP, while urea remains outside it.
It applies only to one grade of fertiliser and fixes subsidy per tonne of crude oil.
It covers all fertilisers, including urea, without reference to nutrient content.
accepted.x: NBS covers 22 grades of decontrolled P&K fertilisers, including DAP, MOP and SSP, and fixes subsidy per kilogram of N, P, K and S nutrients. Urea is outside the scheme.
accepted.tq: Separate the covered P&K grades and nutrients from the excluded fertiliser, urea.
accepted.sec: Subsidies - major heads, explicit vs hidden, NBS, Oil Pool Account  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Oil Pool Account associated with the Administered Price Mechanism was dismantled in:
accepted.x: The Oil Pool Account under the Administered Price Mechanism was dismantled in April 2002.
accepted.tq: Use the precise month-year combination to avoid confusing the reform with neighbouring years.
accepted.sec: Subsidies - major heads, explicit vs hidden, NBS, Oil Pool Account  [APPSC]

accepted.s: After the dismantling of the Oil Pool Account, later under-recoveries of oil companies were compensated through:
accepted.x: Later petroleum under-recoveries were compensated through oil bonds.
accepted.tq: Match the petroleum under-recovery mechanism with its specific compensation instrument.
accepted.sec: Subsidies - major heads, explicit vs hidden, NBS, Oil Pool Account  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following principles was associated with the approach of the Sixteenth Finance Commission towards subsidies?
1. Retaining only well-targeted subsidies
2. Providing exclusion criteria and sunset clauses
3. Permitting off-budget financing of subsidies without restriction
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The approach supports well-targeted subsidies, exclusion criteria and sunset clauses. It does not support unrestricted off-budget financing of subsidies.
accepted.tq: Identify the negative statement that reverses the Commission's transparency and targeting principles.
accepted.sec: Subsidies - major heads, explicit vs hidden, NBS, Oil Pool Account  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In Budget 2026-27, the total subsidy provision was approximately:
accepted.x: The total subsidy provision in Budget 2026-27 was ₹4,54,773 crore, representing a 3.1 per cent decline from the 2025-26 revised estimate.
accepted.tq: Read the exact Budget figure and distinguish it from closely spaced alternatives.
accepted.sec: Subsidies - major heads, explicit vs hidden, NBS, Oil Pool Account  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In Budget 2026-27, food and fertiliser subsidies together accounted for approximately what share of the total subsidy bill?
accepted.x: Food subsidy of ₹2,27,629 crore and fertiliser subsidy of ₹1,70,799 crore together accounted for 87 per cent of the total subsidy bill.
accepted.tq: Combine the two stated major heads and compare their aggregate share with the total bill.
accepted.sec: Subsidies - major heads, explicit vs hidden, NBS, Oil Pool Account  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The major subsidies comprising food, fertiliser and petroleum in Budget 2026-27 were estimated at approximately what share of GDP?
accepted.x: Food, fertiliser and petroleum subsidies together amounted to about ₹4.11 lakh crore, equivalent to 1.0 per cent of GDP.
accepted.tq: Match the aggregate subsidy amount with its stated GDP ratio.
accepted.sec: Subsidies - major heads, explicit vs hidden, NBS, Oil Pool Account  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Centre plus States public expenditure to GDP ratio was approximately what in the Economic Survey 2016-17?
accepted.x: Public expenditure of the Centre and States together was about 28 per cent of GDP in the Economic Survey 2016-17.
accepted.tq: Identify the combined-government ratio rather than a Union-only expenditure ratio.
accepted.sec: Public expenditure trends - expenditure-GDP ratio, largest items, committed expenditure  [APPSC]

accepted.s: According to Union Budget Estimates 2026-27, total expenditure was approximately:
accepted.x: The Union Budget Estimates 2026-27 placed total expenditure at ₹53,47,315 crore, or 13.6 per cent of GDP.
accepted.tq: Use the exact total expenditure figure and avoid confusing it with the revenue or capital components.
accepted.sec: Public expenditure trends - expenditure-GDP ratio, largest items, committed expenditure  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the Union Budget Estimates 2026-27?
o: Revenue expenditure 3.1% of GDP and capital expenditure 10.5% of GDP
Revenue expenditure 7.7% of GDP and capital expenditure 13.6% of GDP
Revenue expenditure 13.6% of GDP and capital expenditure 10.5% of GDP
Revenue expenditure 10.5% of GDP and capital expenditure 3.1% of GDP
accepted.x: Revenue expenditure was estimated at ₹41.25 lakh crore, or 10.5 per cent of GDP, while capital expenditure was ₹12.22 lakh crore, or 3.1 per cent of GDP.
accepted.tq: Keep the revenue and capital ratios paired with their correct expenditure heads.
accepted.sec: Public expenditure trends - expenditure-GDP ratio, largest items, committed expenditure  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In the 2026-27 Union Budget expenditure composition, the largest share was assigned to:
accepted.x: States' share of taxes accounted for 22 per cent of the expenditure composition, followed by interest at 20 per cent and central sector schemes at 17 per cent.
accepted.tq: Read the expenditure composition chart as a ranking question rather than relying on the usual generic largest-item answer.
accepted.sec: Public expenditure trends - expenditure-GDP ratio, largest items, committed expenditure  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following components of Union Budget 2026-27 expenditure in descending order of their stated shares:
A. Defence
B. Central Sector Schemes
C. Interest
D. States' share of taxes
accepted.x: The shares were States' share of taxes 22 per cent, interest 20 per cent, Central Sector Schemes 17 per cent and defence 11 per cent.
accepted.tq: Rank the options by the numerical shares, starting with the largest component.
accepted.sec: Public expenditure trends - expenditure-GDP ratio, largest items, committed expenditure  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Interest payments in Union Budget Estimates 2026-27 were approximately what proportion of total expenditure and revenue receipts, respectively?
accepted.x: Interest payments of ₹14,03,972 crore represented 26 per cent of total expenditure and 40 per cent of revenue receipts.
accepted.tq: Do not reverse the two denominators when comparing the percentages.
accepted.sec: Public expenditure trends - expenditure-GDP ratio, largest items, committed expenditure  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the trend in interest payments as a share of revenue receipts?
accepted.x: Interest payments were 37 per cent of revenue receipts in 2013-14, 42 per cent in 2020-21 and 40 per cent in the 2026-27 estimate.
accepted.tq: Preserve the year-wise order while comparing closely related percentages.
accepted.sec: Public expenditure trends - expenditure-GDP ratio, largest items, committed expenditure  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Committed expenditure consisting of salaries, pensions and interest payments accounted for what proportion of revenue receipts?
accepted.x: Committed expenditure, comprising salaries, pensions and interest payments, was 65.3 per cent of revenue receipts.
accepted.tq: Associate the exact percentage with the complete committed-expenditure group.
accepted.sec: Public expenditure trends - expenditure-GDP ratio, largest items, committed expenditure  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which statement correctly represents the trend in Union revenue expenditure as a percentage of GDP?
o: It declined from 13.6% in FY22 to 3.1% in FY25.
It declined from 13.6% in FY22 to 10.9% in FY25.
It remained unchanged at 13.6% between FY22 and FY25.
It increased from 10.9% in FY22 to 13.6% in FY25.
accepted.x: Revenue expenditure declined from 13.6 per cent of GDP in FY22 to 10.9 per cent in FY25.
accepted.tq: Check both the direction of change and the correct years before selecting the trend.
accepted.sec: Public expenditure trends - expenditure-GDP ratio, largest items, committed expenditure  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The share of revenue expenditure in total Union expenditure changed from 2014-15 to the 2026-27 Budget Estimate as follows:
accepted.x: Revenue expenditure accounted for 88 per cent of total expenditure in 2014-15 and about 77 per cent in the 2026-27 Budget Estimate.
accepted.tq: Identify the direction of the long-term share change rather than confusing it with the committed-expenditure ratio.
accepted.sec: Public expenditure trends - expenditure-GDP ratio, largest items, committed expenditure  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements regarding State government expenditure is correct?
1. States' spending was between 16.15 per cent and 17.49 per cent of GSDP during 2014-24.
2. Revenue expenditure constituted 80-87 per cent of total expenditure.
3. Committed expenditure plus subsidies constituted 51.76 per cent of revenue expenditure in FY24.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements correctly describe the stated expenditure pattern of States: spending of 16.15-17.49 per cent of GSDP, revenue expenditure of 80-87 per cent of total expenditure, and 51.76 per cent for committed expenditure plus subsidies in FY24.
accepted.tq: Verify each numerical range and the specific FY24 percentage before choosing the combined code.
accepted.sec: Public expenditure trends - expenditure-GDP ratio, largest items, committed expenditure  [APPSC]

accepted.s: State government total expenditure as a percentage of GDP changed from FY19 to FY24 in which manner?
accepted.x: Total expenditure of States declined from 15.7 per cent of GDP in FY19 to 15.4 per cent in FY24.
accepted.tq: Compare the two specified years and retain the correct direction of movement.
accepted.sec: Public expenditure trends - expenditure-GDP ratio, largest items, committed expenditure  [APPSC]
